newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says 25 pre-qualified firms for Bayovar sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru says 25 pre-qualified firms for Bayovar sale.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Thursday 25 mining firms had pre-qualified for the February privatization of its Bayovar phosphate deposit.
"The basic rules for the sale have been distributed to the pre-qualified companies, which number at this time 25," the government's privatization chief Jorge Gonzales Izquierdo told Congress.
State miner Minero Peru - reponsible for the February 11 sale - has said various U.S., Canadian and Mexican companies are interested in buying the deposit.

Minero Peru has named 11 firms believed to be seriously interested in bidding for Bayovar, including Canada's Agrium Inc. and Potash Corporation of Saskatchewan; the United States' Agrifos, IMC-Agrico and US Borax; Australia's BHP Minerals; Mexico's Grupo Fertinal and Grupo Penoles; India's Oswal Agro Mills; Chile's Soquimich; and Brazil's Vale do Rio Doce.
In January, the government will announce the minimum price bid for the deposit, which, in the northern department of Piura, has an estimated 262 million tonnes of phosphates' reserves.
Minero Peru also plans to sell the Michiquillay copper and gold deposit, in Cajamarca department, and the Winicocha gold deposit, in Cuzco department, in the first quarter of 1997.

In the second half of 1997, the company, which began privatizing in 1993, plans to offer its Las Bambas copper deposit in Apurimac department and its anthracite coal deposit in La Libertad department.
Izquierdo told Congress he expected Minero Peru to complete the sale of all of its assets in the first half of 1998.
The Minero Peru sales will run parallel to the ongoing, piecemeal privatization of the government's operating mining company, Centromin.
While Centromin's sell-off program includes operating assets as well as deposits, Minero Peru is only selling deposits.
